comparison: Both evaluate claims C27-C29 about plasticity effects. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by model calculations in Figure 4B, treating the plasticity inference as a logical prediction. Peer reviewers rate them UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'Interpreting this as a sign of more plasticity is an overstatement' and identifying it as overinterpretation of model results.

Both evaluate claims C30-C31 about Matérn functions with different smoothness parameters. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED, noting appropriate handling of numerical instability. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, noting the covariance functions 'are not very different' and the test was 'not sufficiently stringent to demonstrate robustness.'

Both evaluate claims C44-C47 about the dual role of density and statistics. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as well-synthesized evidence from literature and current study. Peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED, accepting these as established knowledge without challenge.

Both evaluate claims C70-C71 about block-diagonal covariance assumptions. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with appropriate justification, though notes potential issues for star-nosed mole geometry. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, stating the zero-covariance assumption 'is quite a strong one and seems central to the paper' requiring better justification.

Both evaluate claims about bottleneck width and resource allocation (C4, C14-C18). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with converging analytical and computational evidence. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, requesting major clarifications about model assumptions, biological plausibility, and noting sensitivity to noise in 'numerous tiny tail eigenvalues.'

OpenEval evaluates C20-C22 (activation vs density effects) as SUPPORTED by Figure 2D and analytical derivations. Peer R2 evaluates overlapping claims C20-C24, C26 as UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification of assumptions about correlation structure and noting confusion about terminology like 'activation' vs 'activation ratio.'

OpenEval evaluates C5, C23-C24, C26 (theoretical framework for activation and density) as SUPPORTED with coherent analytical derivations. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims as UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification of assumptions and noting the model makes no distinction between sensor density and exponential decay of covariance functions.

Both evaluate model comparison with star-nosed mole data (C6, C35-C36, C40-C42). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about unknown bottleneck width, overfitting risk, and model flexibility. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, noting the full model has extra degrees of freedom, 'hard to make a strong claim about tiny change in MSE,' and RMSE driven by outlier ray 11.

OpenEval evaluates C72-C75 (core mathematical framework from PCA/efficient coding) as SUPPORTED with standard, well-established derivations. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping C13, C58-C59, C72 as UNCERTAIN, raising major concerns that 'decorrelation is an information maximizing transform only in absence of noise' and finding it 'misleading to claim that the analysis maximizes information without qualification.'

OpenEval evaluates C72-C75 (mathematical framework) as SUPPORTED. Peer R14 evaluates overlapping C73-C75 as UNCERTAIN, requesting more mathematical detail in main text, clarification of cost function and constraints, and noting the model makes no distinction between density and covariance decay.

Both evaluate background claims about sensory systems (C1-C3, C8-C10). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED, accepting these as established empirical motivation without challenge.

Both evaluate claims about bottleneck calculations and visual system (C49-C50, C63). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED though notes the spatial resolution interpretation is indirect. Peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED, accepting the bottleneck discussion and requesting additional citations.

Both evaluate claims linking neural allocation to perceptual acuity (C60-C62). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with sound logical connections. Peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED (including C64), accepting these as established relationships supporting behavioral relevance.

Both evaluate claims C66-C67 about PCA/ICA generalization. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with valid generalization argument. Peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED (grouped with C68-C69), accepting these as appropriate scope definitions.

Both evaluate claims C68-C69 about model limitations. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as appropriate scientific caution. Peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED (grouped with C66-C67), accepting these as appropriate limitations though requesting better clarification of when decorrelation is information-maximizing.

OpenEval evaluates C11-C13 (theoretical motivation from prior literature) as SUPPORTED. Peer R12 evaluates overlapping C11-C12 (grouped with C1-C3, C8-C10) as SUPPORTED, accepting these as established background knowledge.

OpenEval evaluates C58-C59, C43 (decorrelation for early sensory processing) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R6 evaluates overlapping C13, C58-C59, C72 as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about equating efficient coding with decorrelation and the noise-free assumption.

OpenEval evaluates C7, C48 (synthesis about magnification varying with bottleneck width) as SUPPORTED by comprehensive modeling results. Peer R8 evaluates overlapping C48-C50, C63 as SUPPORTED, accepting the bottleneck discussion without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates C19 (gamma parameter effects) as SUPPORTED by Figure 2C calculations. Peer R1 evaluates this claim (grouped with C4-C5, C7, C14-C18) as UNCERTAIN, requesting major clarifications about model assumptions and noting sensitivity issues.

OpenEval evaluates C7, C48 as SUPPORTED synthesis of findings. Peer R1 evaluates C7 (grouped with C4-C5, C14-C19) as UNCERTAIN, requesting major clarifications about assumptions and biological plausibility.
